name: DC Water news releases and public notices (sewer overflow notices)
operator: District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority (DC Water)
waters_covered: District-wide plus DC Water's Potomac Interceptor in MD and VA; named receiving waters per notice
access_detail: HTML list, 10 items per page, ?page=N (0-based); each item has date ('16  August,  2025'), title, teaser and link /about-dc-water/media/news/<slug>. Fetched pages 0-25 (312 items, back to July 2024) into raw/dcwater-news-index-p0-25.json and 18 notice pages into raw/notices/. No RSS: /rss.xml, /news/rss and /about-dc-water/media/news/rss.xml all 404. Email delivery of news releases via the Everbridge sign-up (see dc-dcwater-everbridge-alerts).

sample_record.title: PUBLIC NOTICE: DC Water Advises Public of Sewer Overflow in Northeast DC
sample_record.teaser: DC Water is advising the public of a Sanitary Sewer Overflow (SSO) on Anacostia Ave Northeast and Ponds St at the entrance to the Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens. A ...
sample_record.body_extract: Wastewater periodically continues to overflow from the broken main, with approximately 6,200 gallons of sewer overflows so far.

cadence: Ad hoc. Major SSOs get a notice the same day or next morning (Potomac Interceptor collapse: notice dated 2026-01-19, the evening it was found; Anacostia Force Main: traffic advisory 2025-07-20, overflow notice 2025-07-21; second force-main SSO at 01:40 2025-08-16 noticed the same day). Small SSOs to creeks and CSOs get no news release. No legal deadline for public notice found.
history: Paginated archive; page 25 reaches July 2024. Deeper pages not fetched.
license: Site terms not reviewed; press releases are public statements. The Sanitary Sewer Dashboard page carries a data disclaimer (see dc-dcwater-sso-csv).
legal_basis: No statute or permit clause requires a press release. Permit DC0021199 Part III.B.1.h (Public Notification) covers lights, website, signs and pamphlets for CSOs.
status_reason: The only place DC Water announces large SSOs to the public, but prose HTML with no feed; scrape the list page daily and parse titles containing overflow/SSO/sewage.
notes: Titles to match: 'Sanitary Sewer Overflow', 'Sewer Overflow', 'Potomac Interceptor', 'Force Main'. Mixed in with traffic advisories and corporate news.

name: EPA ECHO Sewer Overflow/Bypass Event data, DC Water permit DC0021199
operator: US EPA (data reported by DC Water)
waters_covered: DC Water collection system incl. the Potomac Interceptor in MD/VA; receiving water is free text (e.g. 'Potomac River', 'Broad Branch', 'soapstone', 'Rock Creek ')
access_detail: Same national ZIPs the pipeline already ingests (pipeline/ingest/echo_sewer_overflow_events.py, STATES set excludes DC today). Used the federal agent's copy of the all-versions ZIP (extract dated 2026-10-30): 184 DC rows, 140 current; joined child tables into raw/echo-sobe-dc0021199-joined.json.

sample_record.sewer_overflow_bypass_description_text: SSO AT 8310 Clara Barton Parkway (PI site  MH 17 and MH 16)

cadence: ECHO refreshes daily. DC lag from event end to report received: median 4 days, 90th percentile 16 days, max 79 (permit: 5-day written report); the PI collapse row was revised until 2026-04-16 (volume 217 -> 242,000,000 gal).
history: DC rows from 2023-03-31 to 2026-09-26 in the 2026-10-30 extract (29 in 2023, 29 in 2024, 46 in 2025, 34 in 2026, current versions).
license: EPA public data; ECHO data downloads, no licence restriction stated.
legal_basis: 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) 24-hour/5-day noncompliance reporting; permit DC0021199 Part II 'Twenty-Four Hour Reporting'; 40 CFR part 127 eReporting.
status_reason: Best structured DC event source: coordinates, times, volumes, receiving water, revisions. Add 'DC' to STATES in the existing ingest; review the PI rows (location in MD, permit DC).
notes: Of 140 current rows, 33 name a receiving water (31 of them in 2025-2026); 50 are basement backups. Missing: the 2025-08-16 Anacostia Force Main SSO announced by DC Water. Receiving-water text needs a DC alias table (soapstone, Soapstone Stream, Hickory Run, Watts Branch Creek, '@PARK RD @PINEY BRANCH PKY NW'). Two CSO-outfall rows (2025-12-01 CSO 024 DWO, 2026-04-15 Canal Rd) contradict the CSO monthly reports' 'no dry weather combined sewer overflow' lines.

sample_record.description: O Street Sewage Pumping Station, SE (pumped Overflow)

fields: monthly: regulator inspection dates, inflatable dam overflow dates and durations, dry weather overflow statement, daily rainfall at 5 gauges
cadence: Quarterly; due the 28th of the month after the quarter (Q3 2026 posted October 2026). Permit Part III Section E.
history: 2020 Q3 onward on the publications page.
license: Public permit report; no terms stated.
legal_basis: Permit DC0021199 Part III.B.1.h.ii(d) website record of CSO events by outfall for the prior quarter; Part III Section E quarterly reports.
status_reason: The legally required public CSO record. Quarter-precision totals per outfall: use as annual/quarterly totals (no event pages). Needs PDF parsing, OCR for some quarters.
notes: Q3 2026 shows a metered 5.54 MG pumped overflow at CSO 010 (O Street PS) into the Anacostia: the first Anacostia CSO volume in the 2026 tables seen. Each monthly section says 'There was no dry weather combined sewer overflow reported during <month>' even for months where EPA SOBE has a DWO row.

name: DC Water CSO Event Indicator Lights (Potomac and Anacostia)
waters_covered: Potomac River (one light, north shore near the mouth of Rock Creek, driven by CSO 021); Anacostia River (four lights: Main Pumping Station, Skimmer Boat Yard, Anacostia Community Boathouse, CSO 019 tunnel overflow structure; driven by the CSO 019 tunnel overflow structure)
access_detail: Physical lights only. The page quotes: 'A red light will be illuminated during a CSO occurrence and a yellow light will be illuminated for 24 hours after CSO has stopped.' No online status of the lights was found (no page, map, API or social feed).
cadence: Real time at the riverside only.
legal_basis: Permit DC0021199 Part III.B.1.h.i: 'Operate a light on the Anacostia River and a light on the Potomac River to notify river users of CSO events ... A light (color A) will be illuminated during a CSO occurrence and a second light (color B) will be illuminated for 24 hours after a CSO has stopped.'
status_reason: Not published online; the SCADA signal behind it (CSO 021, CSO 019) is the real-time feed that does not exist publicly. Ask DC Water for it (owner decision).
notes: The 2002 LTCP (Section 15.8) proposed three colours (A during, B 24 h, C 72 h for significant volume) at three or four locations per river; the permit reduced it to two colours.

name: DC Water Combined Sewer System page (CSO information website required by permit)
access_detail: Fetched (raw/dcwater-css.html). Explains CSOs, lights, '48 potentially active CSO outfalls', links the CSOSheds interactive map, quarterly reports and 'CSO Overlow Predictions Updated Jan 2026.pdf'. Advice quoted: 'For small rainfalls, the effects of CSOs typically last less than 24 hours. For larger rainfalls, greater than 1" of rain, the effects of CSOs on water quality can last up to three days.' Also: 'the District of Columbia Department of Health has imposed a ban on swimming in all rivers and creeks'. DWO reporting: 'promptly call DC Water at 202-612-3400'.
legal_basis: Permit DC0021199 Part III.B.1.h.ii website requirement.
status_reason: Source of the advice text and of the 24 h / up to 3 days wording for the DC rule row; no live status.
notes: EPA's CSO real-time notification page lists 'Washington, DC' linking to dcwater.com/css, but the page itself has no live status.

name: NPDES permit DC0021199 (DC Water, Blue Plains and the combined sewer system), EPA Region 3
access_detail: Scanned 60-page PDF (no text layer); OCR'd locally to raw/law/blue-plains-npdes-permit.ocr.txt. Cover: 'Effective Date: August 26,2018 / Expiration Date: August 23,2023' (ECHO lists 08/25/2023, status administratively continued). No reissued permit found.
status_reason: The only binding public-notification rule for DC CSOs.
notes: Part III.B.1.h Public Notification (quoted in report): (i) lights on the Anacostia and Potomac, colour A during a CSO and colour B 'for 24 hours after a CSO has stopped'; (ii) a website with CSO locations, health threats, 'record of CSO events by outfall with number, average duration and volume for the prior three month calendar quarter based on modeled results', the light system, and 'nature and duration of conditions potentially harmful to users of receiving waters during and after a CSO event'; (iii)/(iv) semi-annual pamphlets in bills and at boathouses; (vi) bulletin for callers; (vii) 'Maintain warning signs at all CSOs.' DWOs: 'Each dry weather overflow confirmed by the Permittee shall be reported to DDOE and EPA Region III within 24 hours.' Part II: noncompliance that may endanger health reported orally within 24 hours and in writing within 5 days to EPA and DOEE. Part II Section E: quarterly public accountability summary reports on the website. No clause requires notice to the public of SSOs.

name: 21 DCMR § 1108 Rivers (swimming prohibition and special swimming events)
access_detail: Section Word file downloaded via the chapter page's DownloadFile link ({7A0EC83E-5430-40C4-959A-CA9BBE071E0E}); text in raw/law/dcmr-21-1108.txt; effective 5/13/2022.
legal_basis: 21 DCMR 1108.1: 'Except as otherwise provided in this section, primary contact recreation shall be prohibited in the Potomac and Anacostia Rivers and Rock Creek until such time as the standards in § 1104.8 for Class A beneficial use are consistently maintained.'
status_reason: The swimming ban, in force; special events need E. coli <= 410 single sample and the Director must refuse if there 'may be a health risk from a known pollution source, including: (1) Combined sewer overflow; (2) Failing sewer infrastructure'.

name: 21 DCMR § 1104 Standards (E. coli criteria, Class A)
access_detail: raw/law/dcmr-21-1104.txt (effective 3/14/2025).
legal_basis: 21 DCMR 1104.8 Table 1: E. coli (MPN/100 mL) Class A single sample value 410; geometric mean of 5 samples over a maximum of 30 days 126. Footnote e: 'The geometric mean criterion shall be used for assessing water quality trends and for permitting. The single sample value criterion shall be used for assessing water quality trends only.'
status_reason: Numeric criteria used by DOEE, DC Health (410) and Anacostia Riverkeeper (126).
